turns.question: The water temperature on one of our pods has gone jumpy - it steps around by a degree or two between readings while everything else on the same instrument looks steady. Where do we start looking?
turns.answer: Start by checking the temperature sensor itself and its power source. A common cause of “jumpy” temperature readings is a dirty sensor surface, which can be cleaned to remove any dirt or oily film【1†"Dirty sensor—remove dirt and oil film."】. Also verify that the batteries are fresh, since weak batteries can produce unstable readings【1†"Weak batteries—replace with new batteries."】. If the sensor and batteries look fine, inspect the sensor’s connections and cables for dirt, looseness, or damage, as poor connections can also cause erratic output【1†"Bad or dirty connection at meter or sensor connections—tighten or clean the connections."】.

USGS temperature measurements should be stored inthe National Water Information System (NWIS) database
Table 6.1–1. 	Troubleshooting guide for temperature measurements.
Symptom 	Possible cause and corrective action
The sensor does not read accurately 	• Dirty sensor—remove dirt and oil film.
• Weak batteries—replace with new batteries.
• Calibration expired—verify or recertify.
Erratic sensor readings 	• Bad or dirty connection at meter or sensor connections—tighten or clean the connections.
• Break in the cables—replace cables, which may require recertification.
• Weak batteries—replace with new batteries.
Readings are slow to stabilize 	• Dirty sensor—clean the sensor to remove dirt and oily film.

turns.question: If it turns out to be the cable, can we just swap it ourselves and carry on?
turns.answer: Yes—you can replace a faulty cable, but the replacement may need to be recertified before the sensor will meet its accuracy specifications【1†"replace cables, which may require recertification."】.
